QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_50

question.text: For comparing two Category II growth-equity AIFs of the same vintage but different distribution pace, which SINGLE metric most robustly captures both realised return AND market-pace context?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** KS-PME compounds each capital call and distribution using the index return to the valuation date and computes a market-adjusted TVPI. Two funds with different distribution paces are made comparable because KS-PME credits each cash flow by its time-in-market index return. KS-PME = 1 means parity with market; > 1 outperformance. IRR alone (A) is pace-insensitive. PIC (C) just measures deployment. Absolute INR (D) ignores fund size and time value. **The Trap:** Gross IRR doesn't adjust for market conditions. PIC only measures capital deployment. Absolute INR doesn't adjust for fund size or vintage. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests KS-PME supremacy. Cambridge's 'Public Market Equivalent Analysis' white paper is the global reference — LP CIOs use KS-PME as the ultimate cross-fund single-number comparator. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In a re-up pitch, lead with KS-PME (vintage-matched, pace-matched) not IRR. A Cat II Manager with KS-PME > 1.3 beats 90% of same-vintage peers even if headline IRR looks average — and sophisticated LPs know this.
